verdicts.note: Self-identifies as a woman throughout; female confirmed.
Explicit: 'mixed sort of schooling', comprehensive school.
Doing aeronautical engineering, stated repeatedly.
Repeatedly affirms being good at and enjoying maths/physics at school; strong.
Variety is the named main appeal; emphatic 'Absolutely'.
Chose engineering to use maths/physics without going 'hard core' into either alone.
Chose it for interesting work vs 'boring' single subject; genuine though intertwined with variety.
Explicit: 'didn't really know what it entailed when I came here'; agree (had partial knowledge) well-calibrated.
No family in industry ('completely unrelated') = strongly disagree.
Sixth-form careers advisor actively steered her to aeronautical engineering; affirmed supportive.
Explicit: 'no... any discouragement from anyone'.
Not going on placement; declined the year out.
Primary stated reason for not going: already has a year out plus work since age 13.

Quote is 'nothing to benefit ME personally'; she explicitly says placement WOULD be invaluable to others and rotation is valuable, weakening the general 'nothing to be gained' claim. Downgrade confidence.
Rejects placement as a job-prospects motivator; only a 'tiny bit' of employability gain = disagree.

Quote is hypothetical ('if you wanted to design fuselages') describing big-company breadth, not her preference. She says she likes 'not being pigeon holed', wants to 'try a bit of this... seeing where I fit in' = don't know.
'I'd much rather be on the shop floor... doing the engineering thing' over managerial paperwork = technical/specialist.
'salary, salary... that's quite a big pull' = very important.
Lists location among job attractors; no emphasis = important (4), well-calibrated.
'training opportunities... wouldn't really bother me' = unimportant.
EO 'wouldn't really attract me to a company'; 'less and less of an issue' = unimportant.
Fears isolation/loneliness, strongly drawn to bigger company for peers; people matter = important.
'quite happy... don't regret anything'; course 'really interesting' = strongly agree.
Variable asks if MORE difficult than EXPECTED. She says hard but 'which I knew it would be... it's exactly what I thought it was' = NOT harder than expected = disagree, not agree.
Chosen quote frames variety within the workload-as-downside passage, not satisfaction; satisfaction inferred from her overall enthusiasm elsewhere. Thin quote, downgrade.
Names the people as the 'best thing'; 'nice spirit amongst everyone' = very satisfied.
'developed me as a person... helped my communication skills'; reinforced by group-work comment.
Views group work positively/'essential'; one mild bad experience. Satisfied (4) reasonable.

Variable is NUMBER OF TEACHING HOURS. Her complaint is overall workload/free-time work; she explicitly downplays contact hours ('25 hours... isn't very much'). Dissatisfaction with teaching hours not supported.
